questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A typical angiosperm anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure in transverse section. In a transverse section, a typical microsporangium itself appears:

options.text: Tetragonal in outline
Near circular in outline
Triangular in outline
Long and rectangular in outline

solution.explanation: NCERT: in a transverse section, a typical microsporangium appears near circular in outline. It is generally surrounded by four wall layers — the epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and the tapetum. The anther as a whole is tetragonal, with a microsporangium at each corner.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Tetragonal' describes the whole anther in transverse section, not one microsporangium; NCERT does not describe the microsporangium as triangular or rectangular in section.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: structures and events — the stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option B: Near circular in outline

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Pollen grains are shed from the anther and must reach the stigma of a pistil for fertilisation. NCERT terms this transfer of pollen grains to the stigma of a pistil:

options.text: Fertilisation
Syngamy
Emasculation
Pollination

solution.explanation: NCERT: in flowering plants, both the male and female gametes are non-motile, so they have to be brought together for fertilisation to occur. Pollination is the mechanism to achieve this objective: the transfer of pollen grains (shed from the anther) to the stigma of a pistil is termed pollination.
steps: Anther → stigma transfer of pollen = pollination
solution.why_others_wrong: Fertilisation and syngamy are fusions of gametes inside the embryo sac, which come after pollination; emasculation is the removal of anthers in artificial hybridisation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: structures and events — pollination
solution.final_answer: Option D: Pollination

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Enclosed within the integuments of an ovule is a mass of cells that have abundant reserve food materials. This mass of cells is the:

options.text: Nucellus
Funicle
Chalaza
Hilum

solution.explanation: NCERT: enclosed within the integuments is a mass of cells called the nucellus. Cells of the nucellus have abundant reserve food materials. Located in the nucellus is the embryo sac or female gametophyte.
steps: Nucellus: food-rich cells; contains the embryo sac
solution.why_others_wrong: The funicle is the stalk that attaches the ovule to the placenta; the hilum is the region where the ovule's body fuses with the funicle; the chalaza is the basal part of the ovule.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: structures and events — the pistil, megasporangium (ovule) and embryo sac
solution.final_answer: Option A: Nucellus

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Much before the actual flower is seen on a plant, several hormonal and structural changes lead to the differentiation and further development of the floral primordium.
Statement II: In the majority of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 3-celled stage.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Floral development and the stage of pollen shedding
solution.explanation: NCERT: several hormonal and structural changes are initiated which lead to the differentiation and further development of the floral primordium; inflorescences then bear floral buds and flowers (Statement I true). In over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 2-celled stage; only in the remaining species is the generative cell divided into two male gametes before shedding (Statement II false).
steps: Floral primordium develops before the flower appears
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', flower – a fascinating organ of angiosperms; pre-fertilisation: structures and events
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a majority of flowering plants, only one of the four megaspores is functional and develops into the female gametophyte. This method of embryo sac formation from a single megaspore is termed:

options.text: Bisporic development
Tetrasporic development
Monosporic development
Free-nuclear development

solution.explanation: NCERT: in a majority of flowering plants, one of the megaspores is functional while the other three degenerate. Only the functional megaspore develops into the female gametophyte (embryo sac). This method of embryo sac formation from a single megaspore is termed monosporic development.
steps: Embryo sac from a single megaspore = monosporic
solution.why_others_wrong: Bi- and tetrasporic would involve two or four megaspores; 'free nuclear' describes the type of nuclear divisions inside the developing embryo sac, not the number of megaspores used.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: structures and events — megasporogenesis and the female gametophyte
solution.final_answer: Option C: Monosporic development

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cleistogamous flowers produce assured seed set even in the absence of pollinators.
Reason (R): Pollen grains are rich in nutrients.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: cleistogamous flowers do not open at all; their anthers dehisce in the flower buds and the pollen comes in contact with the stigma, so they are invariably autogamous and produce assured seed set even without pollinators (A true). Pollen grains are rich in nutrients, which is why pollen tablets are used as food supplements (R true). R has nothing to do with why cleistogamous flowers set seed.
steps: A: closed flowers → self-pollination → assured seed set
R: true, but about pollen as food
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollination; pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In pollen grains that are shed at the 3-celled stage, the generative cell has already given rise to the two male gametes. The generative cell forms them by:

options.text: Mitotic division
Meiotic division
Fusion with the vegetative cell
Budding from the vegetative nucleus

solution.explanation: NCERT: the generative cell is small and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell. In over 60 per cent of angiosperms pollen is shed at the 2-celled stage; in the remaining species, the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to the two male gametes before the pollen grains are shed (3-celled stage).
steps: Generative cell → 2 male gametes by mitosis
solution.why_others_wrong: Meiosis took place earlier, in the pollen mother cell; the gametes do not form by fusion with the vegetative cell or by budding.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: structures and events — pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option A: Mitotic division

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following gives the correct sequence of events in the formation of a typical (monosporic) embryo sac?

options.text: Meiosis of the megaspore mother cell → all four megaspores fuse → three free-nuclear divisions give the 8-nucleate stage → cell walls are laid down, organising the 7-celled embryo sac
Mitosis of the megaspore mother cell → three of the four megaspores degenerate → cell walls are laid down around each new nucleus after every division → 7-celled embryo sac
Meiosis of the megaspore mother cell → three of the four megaspores degenerate → cell walls are laid down after the 4-nucleate stage → one more division gives the 7-celled embryo sac

Meiosis of the megaspore mother cell → three of the four megaspores degenerate → nucleus of the functional megaspore divides to give a 2-nucleate embryo sac → two more free-nuclear divisions give 4- and then 8-nucleate stages → cell walls are laid down, organising the 7-celled embryo sac

solution.explanation: NCERT: the MMC undergoes meiosis to give four megaspores; in most plants one is functional and three degenerate. The nucleus of the functional megaspore divides mitotically to form two nuclei that move to opposite poles (2-nucleate embryo sac). Two more sequential mitotic nuclear divisions give the 4-nucleate and then 8-nucleate stages. These divisions are strictly free nuclear; only after the 8-nucleate stage are cell walls laid down, giving the typical female gametophyte — 8-nucleate and 7-celled.
solution.why_others_wrong: The megaspores do not fuse; the MMC divides by meiosis, not mitosis; and walls are laid down only after the 8-nucleate stage, since the divisions are strictly free nuclear.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: megasporogenesis and the female gametophyte
solution.final_answer: Option D: Meiosis of the megaspore mother cell → three of the four megaspores degenerate → nucleus of the functional megaspore divides to give a 2-nucleate embryo sac → two more free-nuclear divisions give 4- and then 8-nucleate stages → cell walls are laid down, organising the 7-celled embryo sac

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following gives the correct sequence in the development of the male gametophyte in a species that sheds its pollen at the 2-celled stage?

options.text: Pollen mother cell undergoes mitosis → microspore tetrad → pollen grain with a vegetative and a generative cell → generative cell divides by meiosis to form two male gametes

Pollen mother cell undergoes meiosis → microspore tetrad → microspores dissociate as the anther dehydrates → pollen grain with a vegetative and a generative cell is shed → generative cell divides in the pollen tube to form two male gametes
Pollen mother cell undergoes meiosis → microspores dissociate → generative cell divides to form two male gametes → pollen grain is shed at the 3-celled stage
Microspore tetrad → pollen mother cell undergoes meiosis → microspores dissociate → pollen grain is shed with two male gametes

solution.explanation: NCERT: each pollen mother cell undergoes meiosis to form a microspore tetrad. As the anthers mature and dehydrate, the microspores dissociate and develop into pollen grains. A mature pollen grain contains a vegetative and a generative cell; in over 60 per cent of angiosperms it is shed at this 2-celled stage. In these plants, the generative cell divides to form the two male gametes during the growth of the pollen tube in the stigma.
steps: 2-celled shedding → gametes formed in the pollen tube
solution.why_others_wrong: The PMC divides by meiosis and the generative cell by mitosis; a species that sheds 2-celled pollen does not form the male gametes before shedding; and the tetrad is the product, not the starting point, of the PMC's meiosis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: microsporogenesis and pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option B: Pollen mother cell undergoes meiosis → microspore tetrad → microspores dissociate as the anther dehydrates → pollen grain with a vegetative and a generative cell is shed → generative cell divides in the pollen tube to form two male gametes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: After compatible pollination, which of the following gives the correct path of the pollen tube up to the release of the male gametes?

options.text: Emerges through a germ pore → grows through the style → enters the ovule through the chalaza → enters an antipodal cell and releases the male gametes
Emerges through any point of the exine → grows through the ovary wall → enters the ovule through the micropyle → releases the male gametes directly into the central cell

Emerges through a germ pore → grows through the tissues of the stigma and style → reaches the ovary → enters the ovule through the micropyle → enters a synergid through the filiform apparatus and releases the male gametes
Emerges through a germ pore → grows through the stigma and style → enters the ovule through the micropyle → enters the egg cell through the filiform apparatus

solution.explanation: NCERT: following compatible pollination, the pollen grain germinates on the stigma to produce a pollen tube through one of the germ pores. The tube grows through the tissues of the stigma and style and reaches the ovary. Pollen tubes, after reaching the ovary, enter the ovule through the micropyle and then enter one of the synergids through the filiform apparatus; the filiform apparatus present at the micropylar part of the synergids guides the entry of the pollen tube. The male gametes are released into the cytoplasm of the synergid.
solution.why_others_wrong: The tube enters the ovule through the micropyle, not the chalaza; it emerges through a germ pore, where sporopollenin is absent; and the filiform apparatus belongs to the synergids, not to the egg or the antipodals.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollen-pistil interaction; double fertilisation
solution.final_answer: Option C: Emerges through a germ pore → grows through the tissues of the stigma and style → reaches the ovary → enters the ovule through the micropyle → enters a synergid through the filiform apparatus and releases the male gametes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (value given in NCERT) with List-II (what it refers to).

List-I:
A. About 30 genera
B. Over 60 per cent
C. About 25–50 micrometres
D. −196 °C

List-II:
I. Temperature of the liquid nitrogen in which pollen grains are stored in pollen banks
II. Usual diameter of pollen grains
III. Share of angiosperms whose pollen is shed at the 2-celled stage
IV. Number of genera, mostly monocotyledons, to which pollination by water is limited

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

solution.concept: Numbers in NCERT's account of pollen and pollination
solution.explanation: NCERT: pollination by water is quite rare and limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons (A-IV); in over 60 per cent of angiosperms pollen is shed at the 2-celled stage (B-III); pollen grains are generally spherical, measuring about 25–50 micrometres in diameter (C-II); pollen of many species can be stored for years in liquid nitrogen at −196 °C (D-I).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes interchange the two figures about pollen shedding and water pollination, the size and the shedding share, or the size and the storage temperature.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollen grain; pollination
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Pollen grains of rice and wheat lose their viability within 30 minutes of their release.
Reason (R): The intine of a pollen grain is a thin and continuous layer made up of cellulose and pectin.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the period for which pollen grains remain viable is highly variable; in rice and wheat they lose viability within 30 minutes of release, while in some members of Rosaceae, Leguminoseae and Solanaceae they remain viable for months (A true). The inner wall, the intine, is a thin and continuous layer made of cellulose and pectin (R true). NCERT links viability to the species and to temperature and humidity, not to the composition of the intine, so R does not explain A.
steps: A: rice and wheat pollen viable < 30 min (true)
R: intine of cellulose and pectin (true)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In NCERT's activity to study pollen germination, pollen from flowers such as pea, chickpea, Crotalaria, balsam or Vinca is dusted on a drop of sugar solution on a glass slide. After about how long is the slide observed under the low power lens to see pollen tubes coming out of the pollen grains?

options.text: About 24 hours
About 2–3 days
About one week
About 15–30 minutes

solution.explanation: NCERT: dust some pollen from flowers such as pea, chickpea, Crotalaria, balsam and Vinca on a glass slide containing a drop of sugar solution (about 10 per cent). After about 15–30 minutes, observe the slide under the low power lens of the microscope; you are likely to see pollen tubes coming out of the pollen grains.
solution.why_others_wrong: Pollen tubes appear within minutes in this activity; periods of a day or more are far longer than NCERT states (and the pollen of some species loses viability within 30 minutes).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollination — pollen-pistil interaction
solution.final_answer: Option D: About 15–30 minutes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a dicotyledonous embryo, the portion of the embryonal axis above the level of the cotyledons is the epicotyl, which terminates with the plumule or stem tip.
Statement II: In the embryo of a grass, the coleoptile is the undifferentiated sheath that encloses the radicle and the root cap.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Parts of dicot and grass embryos
solution.explanation: NCERT: in a typical dicot embryo, the portion of the embryonal axis above the level of the cotyledons is the epicotyl, which terminates with the plumule or stem tip (Statement I true). In the grass embryo, the radicle and root cap are enclosed in an undifferentiated sheath called the coleorhiza; the coleoptile is a hollow foliar structure that encloses the shoot apex and a few leaf primordia (Statement II false).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: structures and events — embryo
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Water hyacinth and water lily are aquatic plants, yet they are not pollinated by water.
Reason (R): In these plants, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Not all aquatic plants are water-pollinated
solution.explanation: NCERT: not all aquatic plants use water for pollination; in a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in most land plants. R gives the reason for A.
steps: So pollinated by insects or wind, not water
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollination — agents of pollination

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the micropylar and chalazal ends of the ovule and the embryo sac are correct?

(a) The egg apparatus is situated at the micropylar end of the embryo sac.
(b) The three antipodal cells are situated at the chalazal end.
(c) The megaspore mother cell is differentiated in the micropylar region of the nucellus.
(d) The filiform apparatus is present at the micropylar tip of the synergids.
(e) The pollen tube enters the ovule through the chalaza.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (c) and (d) only
(b), (c), (d) and (e) only

solution.concept: Polarity of the ovule and embryo sac
solution.explanation: NCERT: ovules generally differentiate a single MMC in the micropylar region of the nucellus (c). In the mature embryo sac, three cells are grouped at the micropylar end to form the egg apparatus (a), and three cells at the chalazal end are the antipodals (b). The synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip, the filiform apparatus (d). The pollen tube enters the ovule through the micropyle, not the chalaza (e false).
steps: Micropylar end: MMC, egg apparatus, filiform apparatus, pollen-tube entry
solution.why_others_wrong: (e) is false, so every option with it is wrong; '(a), (c) and (d) only' leaves out the chalazal position of the antipodals (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: megasporogenesis and the female gametophyte; double fertilisation
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (seed named in NCERT) with List-II (where the food reserve of the mature seed lies).

List-I:
A. Pea
B. Castor
C. Beet
D. Coconut

List-II:
I. Endosperm that is partly free-nuclear (liquid) and partly cellular
II. A persistent remnant of the nucellus (perisperm)
III. A part of the endosperm that persists in the mature seed
IV. Thick, swollen cotyledons, the endosperm having been completely consumed

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

solution.explanation: NCERT: in pea, groundnut and beans the endosperm is completely consumed by the developing embryo before seed maturation (non-albuminous seeds), and the cotyledons are thick and swollen with stored food (A-IV). Castor, like wheat, maize and barley, retains a part of the endosperm that is not completely used up during embryo development (albuminous seed) (B-III). In some seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of the nucellus persist; this residual, persistent nucellus is the perisperm (C-II). In coconut, the coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm made up of thousands of nuclei and the surrounding white kernel is cellular endosperm (D-I).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes interchange the non-albuminous pea with albuminous castor, the castor endosperm with the beet perisperm, or the beet perisperm with the coconut endosperm.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: structures and events — endosperm; seed
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination, since it involves a pollinating agent.
Reason (R): In geitonogamy, pollen grains are transferred to the stigma of a flower borne on a different plant.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: geitonogamy is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the SAME plant. Although it is functionally cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent (A true), it is genetically similar to autogamy, since the pollen grains come from the same plant. Transfer to a flower of a different plant is xenogamy, so R is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollination — kinds of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a two-celled pollen grain, the generative cell is the larger of the two cells and has abundant food reserve.
Reason (R): The generative cell is small and spindle-shaped, with dense cytoplasm and a nucleus, and it floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus; the generative cell is small and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell, and it is spindle-shaped with dense cytoplasm and a nucleus. A attributes the vegetative cell's features to the generative cell (false); R is NCERT's description of the generative cell (true).
steps: Vegetative cell: big, food reserve, irregular nucleus
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The two male gametes of a pollen grain are genetically identical, since both arise by mitosis from a single generative cell.
Statement II: The four megaspores formed from one megaspore mother cell are genetically identical to one another, since all four come from a single cell.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to the two male gametes, so they carry the same genetic information (Statement I true). The megaspore mother cell, however, undergoes MEIOSIS to produce four megaspores; meiosis separates homologous chromosomes (and their alleles), so the four megaspores of a heterozygous plant are not all genetically identical (Statement II false). Coming from a single cell does not make the products identical when the division is meiotic.
steps: Male gametes: mitosis of one cell → identical
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollen grain; megasporogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT describes two developmental processes in the ovule in which nuclear divisions are not immediately followed by cell wall formation (free-nuclear divisions). These two processes are:

options.text: Development of the embryo sac from the functional megaspore, and the most common type of endosperm development
Meiosis of the megaspore mother cell, and the development of the embryo from the zygote
Development of the embryo from the zygote, and the formation of the seed coat from the integuments
Formation of the microspore tetrad, and the development of the embryo sac from the functional megaspore

solution.explanation: NCERT: the nucleus of the functional megaspore divides mitotically, and two more sequential divisions give the 8-nucleate stage; these divisions are strictly free nuclear, i.e. not followed immediately by cell wall formation. In the most common type of endosperm development, the primary endosperm nucleus undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give free nuclei; cell wall formation follows later and the endosperm becomes cellular.
steps: Embryo sac: 2 → 4 → 8 free nuclei, then walls
Endosperm (common type): free nuclei, then cellular
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT does not describe the embryo, the seed coat or the meiosis of spore mother cells as free nuclear; the microspore tetrad forms in the anther, not in the ovule.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: female gametophyte; post-fertilisation: endosperm
solution.final_answer: Option A: Development of the embryo sac from the functional megaspore, and the most common type of endosperm development

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A typical angiosperm anther (bilobed, each lobe dithecous) releases 2560 pollen grains in all, and its microsporangia contain equal numbers of pollen mother cells. If every pollen mother cell completed microsporogenesis normally and every microspore became a pollen grain, how many pollen mother cells were present in each microsporangium?

solution.concept: From pollen grains back to pollen mother cells
solution.explanation: A bilobed anther with dithecous lobes has 2 × 2 = 4 microsporangia, so each microsporangium yields 2560/4 = 640 pollen grains. Each pollen mother cell gives a tetrad of four microspores, i.e. four pollen grains, so each microsporangium had 640/4 = 160 pollen mother cells.
solution.why_others_wrong: 640 is the number of pollen grains per microsporangium (the tetrad step is skipped); 320 counts only two microsporangia per anther; 40 divides by four once too often.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: the stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain; microsporogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: 160

solution.concept: Binomial representation of a monohybrid cross

solution.final_answer: Option A: (1/2 T + 1/2 t)² = 1/4 TT + 1/2 Tt + 1/4 tt

A sex-linked dominant disorder carried on the Y chromosome
A disorder caused by an increase in a whole set of chromosomes
An inborn error of metabolism, inherited as an autosomal recessive trait

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Mendel published his work in 1865, but it remained unrecognised till 1900. Which of the following does NCERT give as one of the reasons?

options.text: His experiments were based on too small a sample of plants
Communication was not easy in those days, and his work could not be widely publicised
His results were contradicted by Morgan's experiments on Drosophila
He studied characters that did not show contrasting traits

solution.explanation: NCERT gives several reasons: communication was not easy (as it is now) in those days and his work could not be widely publicised; his concept of factors as stable and discrete units was not accepted as an explanation for the apparently continuous variation seen in nature; the use of mathematics to explain biological phenomena was new and unacceptable to many biologists; and he could not provide any physical proof for the existence of factors.
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT credits Mendel with a large sampling size and with characters showing contrasting traits; Morgan's work came decades later and supported, not contradicted, Mendelian inheritance.

solution.explanation: Rr × Rr gives 1/4 RR (red) : 1/2 Rr (pink) : 1/4 rr (white). Pink = 1/2 × 400 = 200.

So changing a DNA segment changes the chromosome

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A pea plant heterozygous for seed shape and seed colour (RrYy; the two genes assort independently) is self-pollinated, and 1600 seeds are obtained. How many seeds are expected to be heterozygous for exactly one of the two genes?

solution.concept: Genotype classes in a dihybrid F2
solution.explanation: For each gene, Rr × Rr gives 1/2 heterozygous and 1/2 homozygous (likewise for Y). Exactly one heterozygous = P(Rr)·P(YY or yy) + P(RR or rr)·P(Yy) = 1/2·1/2 + 1/2·1/2 = 1/2. Expected = 1/2 × 1600 = 800.
solution.shortcut: Exactly one of two independent 1/2 events: 2 × 1/4 = 1/2.
solution.why_others_wrong: 400 counts seeds heterozygous for both genes (1/4); 1200 counts seeds heterozygous for at least one gene (3/4); 200 counts only one of the two ways (e.g. Rr with homozygous Y) and halves it again.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes: law of independent assortment

Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

A is true but R is false.

solution.concept: Predicting a cross under incomplete dominance
solution.explanation: Red is RR and pink is Rr. Every gamete of the red parent carries R, so every offspring is RR (red) or Rr (pink), in a 1 : 1 ratio. A white flower needs rr, which requires r from both parents; because each offspring gets R from the red parent, rr cannot arise. R therefore explains A.
steps: Offspring RR or Rr → red or pink

questions.subject: Botany

For which of the following can the genotype be stated with certainty from the phenotype alone?

(a) A person with blood group AB

(a), (b) and (d) only
(a), (d) and (e) only
(b), (c) and (e) only

A pink snapdragon must be Rr, since under incomplete dominance the heterozygote has its own phenotype (d). Blood group A may be IᴬIᴬ or Iᴬi (c), and a tall pea plant may be TT or Tt (e) — which is why a test cross is needed to find the genotype of a plant with the dominant phenotype.
steps: A → IᴬIᴬ or Iᴬi; tall → TT or Tt

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In humans, each pregnancy has an equal (50 per cent) chance of producing a male or a female child. A couple has four children. What is the probability that exactly two of them are sons and two are daughters, in any order of birth?

solution.concept: Probability of a mix of sons and daughters
solution.explanation: NCERT: in each pregnancy there is always a 50 per cent probability of a male or a female child. For four children there are 2⁴ = 16 equally likely birth orders. The number of orders with exactly two sons is 4C2 = 6, so the probability is 6/16 = 3/8.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/2 assumes 'half sons' is the most likely outcome with probability 1/2; 1/16 counts only one particular order; 1/4 has no basis in the count of orders.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination: sex determination in humans
solution.final_answer: Option C: 3/8

Two
Four
Three

The dominant trait is a colour for flower colour (violet), pod colour (green) and seed colour (yellow): three characters.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Take NCERT's model of human skin colour controlled by three genes A, B and C, in which every dominant allele adds equally to the colour. A person of genotype AaBbCc marries a person of genotype AABBcc. What fraction of their children are expected to carry exactly four dominant alleles?

solution.concept: Additive alleles with one parent of fixed contribution
solution.explanation: Every gamete of the AABBcc parent is ABc, carrying two dominant alleles. The AaBbCc parent passes 0–3 dominant alleles, each gene independently with probability 1/2, giving 1/8, 3/8, 3/8, 1/8 for 0, 1, 2, 3. A child with four dominant alleles needs exactly two from the AaBbCc parent: probability 3C2/8 = 3/8.

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', polygenic inheritance

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A woman with normal vision who is a carrier of red-green colour blindness marries a man with normal colour vision. They have two children. What is the probability that one of them is a colour-blind son and the other is a carrier daughter, in either order of birth?

solution.explanation: For each child: P(son) = 1/2 and a son is colour blind if he gets the mother's affected X (1/2), so P(colour-blind son) = 1/4. P(daughter) = 1/2, and every daughter gets the father's normal X; she is a carrier if she gets the mother's affected X (1/2), so P(carrier daughter) = 1/4. Two orders are possible: 2 × (1/4 × 1/4) = 1/8.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/16 takes only one birth order; 1/4 is the probability for a single child of one type; 1/2 is the chance that a son is colour blind, not the combined probability.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders — colour blindness
solution.final_answer: Option B: 1/8

questions.question_text:
Consider four species in each of which the diploid female has 20 chromosomes in her somatic cells. Sex is determined in them by the XO, XY, ZW and haplodiploid mechanisms described in NCERT, respectively. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) In the XO species, a somatic cell of the male has 19 chromosomes.
(b) In the XY species, a somatic cell of the male has 20 chromosomes.
(c) In the haplodiploid species, the male has 10 chromosomes.

Two parents with normal phenotype are both heterozygous carriers of phenylketonuria. Which of the following statements are correct?

NCERT: the affected individual lacks an enzyme that converts phenylalanine into tyrosine (b); phenylalanine accumulates and is converted into phenylpyruvic acid and other derivatives, whose accumulation in the brain results in mental retardation (c).

Coding strand

Heavy DNA was distinguished from normal DNA by centrifugation in a caesium chloride density gradient. NCERT notes that ¹⁵N is not a radioactive isotope and can be separated from ¹⁴N only based on densities — which is exactly why density, not radioactivity, was used.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the experimental proof

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty purified biochemicals such as proteins, DNA and RNA from heat-killed S cells to see which of them could transform live R cells into S cells.

They discovered that DNA alone from S bacteria caused R bacteria to become transformed and concluded that DNA is the hereditary material, but not all biologists were convinced (Statement II true). The unequivocal proof came later from Hershey and Chase.

Concluded DNA; not all were convinced

A. Bacteria infected with phages grown on radioactive sulphur were not radioactive
B. Digesting the transforming extract with DNase inhibited transformation
C. ¹⁵N-DNA showed only hybrid density after one generation in ¹⁴N medium, and equal hybrid and light DNA after two generations
D. Mice injected with heat-killed S strain plus live R strain bacteria died, and live S strain bacteria were recovered from them

List-II:
I. The R strain bacteria had been transformed by a 'transforming principle' from the heat-killed S strain
II. DNA replicates semiconservatively
III. DNA is the transforming principle
IV. The viral protein did not enter the bacteria

options.text: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

Increase exponentially

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A population grows according to the logistic model, dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K], with r = 0.5 per year. When the population has 200 individuals, its growth rate is 80 individuals per year. What is the carrying capacity (K) of the habitat?

solution.concept: Solving the logistic equation for K
solution.explanation: Under exponential growth the rate would be rN = 0.5 × 200 = 100 per year. The actual rate is 80, so (K − N)/K = 80/100 = 0.8. Then N/K = 0.2 and K = 200/0.2 = 1000.
solution.shortcut: (K − N)/K = actual rate ÷ rN; then K = N ÷ (1 − that fraction).
solution.why_others_wrong: 250 treats N/K (instead of (K − N)/K) as 0.8; 800 is K − N, not K; 360 uses (K − N)/N in place of (K − N)/K.
